sections.text: But he, O Mighty One, who understands correctly the relation of the Qualities to action, is not attached to the act, for he perceives that it is merely the action and reaction of the Qualities among themselves.
Those who do not understand the Qualities are interested in the act. Still, the wise man who knows the truth should not disturb the mind of him who does not.
Therefore, surrendering thy actions unto Me, thy thoughts concentrated on the Absolute, free from selfishness and without anticipation of reward, with mind devoid of excitement, begin thou to fight.

We had been discussing chapter three, Karma Yoga, Yoga of Actions. And so far we have learned that act we must because we are part of this Prakriti. The Prakriti functions because each individual constituent parts work with each other.
Just as we have seen in a cycle of rain during the summer, the ocean water becomes clouds and then clouds become rain and the cycle continues. So there is a cycle in this Prakriti which is dependent on its constituent parts, the Prakriti. This manifest world works because each constituent part work with each other.
We being part of this Prakriti, we have our own duties and we need to fulfill their duties. So the advice is perform all your ordained duties, duties which come with the roles which I take in my life. I take a role of a father, role of a husband, role of an employer, an employee, a son.
Whatever role I take, I should perform those actions. So once I understood that this is a part of my duty, I have to continue acting. But then I have come to realize that these actions create bondage.
The bondage of actions and reactions, the reward and punishment. So how do I get out of this? Bhagwan said, act without attachment. If you act with the sense of doership, you are responsible for your actions.
And therefore either you will get the credit for it or a punishment for it. So act without attachment and you will not be bound by your actions. And then the next thing we have seen is that even though I consider that I have nothing more to do now I have achieved everything I need to achieve, it will still continue to act because other people are following your example.
As human beings, we have tendency to follow others to act in our life. We need some role model, we need some guidance, we need some standards. And those standards are other people whom I consider to be my role models.
I follow them and I become role model for others. And therefore, at any given time I should be acting in appropriate manner. So others who are following me get the right role model standard to act for themselves.
Once I considered that Im not attached And Im working. Im working for the Loka Sangram, for the welfare of the society. Bhagawan said, even you can look at my own example.
As the Creator, I have nothing to gain in these three worlds. But I continue to work as the law giver and law enforcer in this universe. This universe is never without laws.
There are no weakens in our natural laws. Law of physics doesnt stop functioning because now its the leap year on 29th of February. I dont know what to do.
There is no exception in nature because the Creator remained as the lawgiver and law enforcer in this universe. So we want to look at I as the Creator. Even though I have nothing to gain, I continue to work.
Because if I do not work, this world will cease to exist. The cycle of creation, maintenance and destruction continues because the Creator continues to support it. That substratum which creates the substratum for this universe is always present in the universe to function.
I, as the part of the Parakrati, should follow that lead and do the same. Continue to act even when I dont consider that I have anything to gain just for the welfare of the society. Even when you consider that other people are acting with attachment.
Now I have come to the conclusion that the best way to act in this world is one. Do my duties as ordained by my roles I play, but act without attachment. So have no attachment to your actions and perform actions.
But I know that the world is not made up of all those detached sannyasis. The people needs motivation for them to act. Their motivation may be the goals they want to achieve in their life, their attachment to their actions, their passions.
I, as the Gnani, have a responsibility to make sure that they dont get confused by this high philosophy. So the next verse says, Na Buddhi Bhedam Janayed Agnanam Karma Sanginam. Its a great responsibility on a person who has achieved knowledge that with my knowledge I dont confuse others.
You know, in our Gita class, the one common thing we hear is, Im more confused now than I was before I came to this class. The more you know, the more you realize how much you dont know. And thats a biggest responsibility in the part of the wise person. To guide the society in a right manner so that people dont take the wrong message from your advice.
One person was an alcoholic, so his father or teacher wanted to give an example and said, Let me show you what alcohol does to you. He takes a glass of alcohol, puts a little worm in it, and the worm obviously after a while dies. Did you see what happened? Yes, yes, I understood what happened. If I drink alcohol, all the worms in my stomach will die! Another person was trying to find out where the brain of a cockroach is. He was a researcher, obviously. Im going to find out where the brain of the cockroach is in his body. So he puts food in front of the cockroach; the cockroach runs towards the food. So he figures out the cockroach does have a brain.
Now let me find out where the brain is. He breaks one leg -- the cockroach limps towards the food. It still has a brain; it was not in that leg.
He breaks another leg -- it still limps towards the food. So the brain was not in that leg either. He breaks the last leg, and the cockroach cant move towards the food.
He says, I figured out the brain was in the last leg which I broke. From your observations and conclusions and the advice that you hear, unless youre prepared for that, you may come to the wrong conclusion. So its the great responsibility on the teacher and the wise people to guide the society appropriately without confusing them. Nabuddi Vedam Janayat Agnaram Karma Sanghi naam.
The ignorant people who are working in this world with attachment -- you should not create confusion in their minds so they stop working. There was a time when some philosophies made people give up everything and become a sannyasi or a monk. Is that the real goal of life? Well, after all is figured out, society just cannot function like that.
If all the young people become sannyasis, who would support the Social Security for people like me who will be retiring? We need people to work so you should not unsettle them. Josayat Sarvakarmani Vidhvan Yuktaha Samacharan For a Vidhvan person, the one who is knowledgeable and is Yukta who is balanced. He knows how to motivate people.
And if they are working with an attachment, encourage them to work. Joshayed Sarva -- somehow engage all of them in actions so that activity doesnt stop. Because if they are acting, there is a chance that sometime they will understand what is the right way to act.
If I am driving in a wrong direction, if I stop driving, I will never reach the right destination. But if I continue driving and then ask somebody and find a direction, then continue driving, I will reach my destination all the time. The operative word is driving. As long as I keep driving and then correct my direction, Ill find the destination.
So it is up to us not to confuse our children. People who listen to us and say this is of no value. What are you going to gain in life? And thats not the way to guide the society.
So for anybody who has the criticism that Hinduism teaches pessimism -- it teaches action consistently, all throughout your life. There is no discussion of retirement here. Bhagavan says, please make sure as a Vidvan person that all people are engaged in actions, because activity is the signature of nature.
Prakrutehe kriyamanani gunaihi karmani sarvasah. Then where is this confusion coming between the one who is acting with an attachment, one who is acting without an attachment. Why the one acting without an attachment is more efficient.
One with acting with an attachment is less efficient. The reason for me to act without attachment is not to detach myself from whats happening but to become more efficient in what Im doing. The more I get attached, the more My mental energy will be dissipated into the worries about what will come out of my actions.
That I will be employing one third of my energy into what may come out of my actions. One-third of my energy goes into what happened last time when I did this, and only one-third of my energy is available for the present. The last proposal I did, I did not win it. Am I going to win this one? That will take away my complete focus on what needs to be done.
Therefore detachment is necessary so that I focus on the present only and function fully in it. But where is this confusion coming for me where I get attached to my actions and it says this ignorance about how the world works. The actions in this world are working by their own nature.
Prakrutehi kriyamanani gunehi karmani sarvasah. All actions performed in this universe are performed because of the gunas of the prakriti of the objects. But I on the other hand think I am the doer.
Ahankara removed atma out of my ignorance by my ego. Karta aham ithimanyate I think I am the doer. Even though guna gunesuvarthantaha -- the gunas interact with the gunas -- we are not islands by ourselves.
We cannot function by ourselves. If everybody moves away from this town and I am the only one left, for a few days it will be very fun because I could walk into Starbucks, nobody can stop me, get a cup of coffee myself, go to the food aisle and get whatever grocery I want. After some time, there wont be anything to do for me, because theres nobody else doing anything for me.
I am surviving because other people are doing their part. Therefore Im functioning as Im functioning. Once I come to that conclusion -- that things are working because these constituent parts of this Prakriti are working with each other -- then I will not develop the ego that I am the doer.
I go to the lab, take hydrogen and oxygen, put them together, and they become water. Now I say, I created water. No, no, Rajan -- hydrogen and oxygen acted on each other and they behaved as per their qualities to create water. You are just a mere agent to put them together.
So you are not the doer. You are just a Nimitta, Matra, Ahanka, ra, Vimu, dhatma, Karta, ahamiti many. He starts thinking that I am the doer.
Whereas the actions are performed by the Prakruti by its own nature. Everything in this Prakriti has sattva, rajas and Tamas. The basic ingredients in each thing.
Those ingredients when they come in contact with each other they function according to their own nature. So two atoms come together. No atomic scientist to do engineered to do anything.
Those atoms will act with each other according to their own gunas. Prakrutehe guna, Sammudaha, sajante guna, karma. So one who is ignorant about this nature of Prakriti in the Gunas of Prakriti he gets attached to the actions.
When I do something and then I get success. Im now attached to my actions. Because I think I achieved this success.
I forget that what I submitted as my project There are about 18 people in my office has to work on it.

Verse 30 is one of the most complete instructions on Karma Yoga in the entire Gita: Mayi sarvani karmani sannyasya adhyatma-chetasa, nirashir nirmamo bhutva yudhyasva vigata-jvarah. Surrender all actions to Me, with mind fixed on the Self, free from desire, free from the sense of mine, and fight without the fever of anxiety. Every element of this instruction is practical: offer actions to the Divine, keep awareness on your true nature, release craving for results, drop possessiveness, and act without mental agitation.
The phrase vigata-jvarah (without fever) is particularly evocative. Fever represents the restless, burning anxiety that accompanies attachment. When we are attached to outcomes, we experience the fever of anticipation, the fever of worry, the fever of disappointment. Krishna prescribes action without this fever - calm, steady engagement with whatever needs to be done.
Today, before you begin your work, pause and consciously offer your actions to something greater - God, the universe, the welfare of all beings. Set your intention: These actions are not for my egos gratification but are offered as service. Throughout the day, check in: Is there fever in my work? Am I anxious about outcomes? When you notice the fever rising, remember: Guna guneshu vartanta - the qualities of nature are simply interacting with the qualities of nature. You, the witness, are untouched. Then return to action with renewed calm. In the evening, reflect: How did working with this attitude change my experience of the day?
